lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: name: ask-matt

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: description: Ask which skill or flow fits your situation. A router over the skills in this repo.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: disable-model-invocation: true

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: # Ask Matt

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: You don't remember every skill, so ask.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: A **flow** is a path through the skills. Most paths run along one **main flow**, and two **on-ramps** merge onto it. Everything else is standalone, or a vocabulary layer that runs underneath.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ## The main flow: idea → ship

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: The route most work travels. You have an idea and want it built.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: 1. **`/grill-with-docs`** — sharpen the idea by interview. Start here when you **have a codebase**: it's stateful, retaining what it learns in `CONTEXT.md` and ADRs. (No codebase? Use `/grill-me` — see Standalone. Both run the same `/grilling` primitive; `grill-with-docs` is the one that leaves a paper trail.)

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: 2. **Branch — can you settle every question in conversation?** If a question needs a runnable answer (state, business logic, a UI you have to see), detour through a prototype, bridged by **`/handoff`** in both directions (see Crossing sessions):

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - **`/handoff`** out, then open a fresh session against that file,

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - **`/prototype`** to answer the question with throwaway code,

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - **`/handoff`** back what you learned, and reference it from the original idea thread.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: 3. **Branch — is this a multi-session build?**

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - **Yes** → **`/to-prd`** (turn the thread into a PRD) → **`/to-issues`** (split the PRD into independently-grabbable issues). Because the issues are independent, **clear context between each one**: start a fresh session per issue and kick off **`/implement`** by passing it the PRD and the single issue to work on.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - **No** → **`/implement`** right here, in the same context window.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Either way, **`/implement`** builds each issue by driving **`/tdd`** internally — one red-green slice at a time — then closes out by running **`/code-review`**, a two-axis review (Standards + Spec) of the diff, before committing. Reach for **`/tdd`** on its own when you just want to build a concrete behaviour test-first without a full spec, and **`/code-review`** on its own whenever you want to review a branch or PR against a fixed point.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ### Context hygiene

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Keep steps 1–3 in **one unbroken context window** — don't compact or clear until after `/to-issues` — so the grilling, PRD, and issues all build on the same thinking. Each `/implement` then starts fresh, working from the issue.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: The limit on this is the **[smart zone](https://www.aihero.dev/ai-coding-dictionary/smart-zone)**: the window (~120k tokens on state-of-the-art models) within which the model still reasons sharply. If a session approaches it before `/to-issues`, don't push on degraded — `/handoff` and continue in a fresh thread.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ## On-ramps

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: A starting situation that generates work, then merges onto the main flow.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - **Bugs and requests piling up** → **`/triage`**. It moves issues through triage roles and produces agent-ready issues, which **`/implement`** later picks up.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Triage is only for issues **you didn't create** — bug reports, incoming feature requests, anything that arrives raw. Issues that `/to-issues` produced are already agent-ready, so **don't triage them**.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - **Something's broken** → **`/diagnosing-bugs`**. For the hard ones: the bug that resists a first glance, the intermittent flake, the regression that crept in between two known-good states. It refuses to theorise until it has a **tight feedback loop** — one command that already goes red on *this* bug — then fixes with a regression test. Its post-mortem hands off to **`/improve-codebase-architecture`** when the real finding is that there's no good seam to lock the bug down.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ## Codebase health

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Not feature work — upkeep.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - **`/improve-codebase-architecture`** — run whenever you have a spare moment to keep the codebase good for agents to operate in. It surfaces **deepening opportunities**; picking one _generates an idea_ you can take into the main flow at `/grill-with-docs`. It's the survey that finds the candidates; **`/codebase-design`** (below) is the bench you design the chosen one on.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ## Vocabulary underneath

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Two model-invoked references that run *beneath* the other skills — each the single source of truth for its vocabulary. Reach for them directly when the **words**, not the process, are the problem; or let the skills above pull them in.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - **`/domain-modeling`** — sharpen the project's *domain* language: challenge a fuzzy term, resolve an overloaded word ("account" doing three jobs), record a hard-to-reverse decision as an ADR. It's the active discipline `/grill-with-docs` drives to keep `CONTEXT.md` a clean glossary.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - **`/codebase-design`** — the deep-module vocabulary (module, interface, depth, seam, adapter, leverage, locality) for designing a module's *shape*: a lot of behaviour behind a small interface at a clean seam. `/tdd` and `/improve-codebase-architecture` both speak it.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ## Crossing sessions

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - **`/handoff`** — when a thread is full or you need to branch off (e.g. into a `/prototype` session), this compacts the conversation into a markdown file. You don't continue in place — you **open a new session and reference that file** to carry the context across. It's the bridge between context windows, in either direction. Use it when you want a **fresh session** but need the **current conversation preserved**.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - **`/compact`** (built-in) — stay in the **same conversation**, letting the earlier turns be summarized. Use it at **intentional breaks between phases**, when you don't mind losing the verbatim history. Don't compact mid-phase — the agent can lose its way. `/handoff` forks; `/compact` continues.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ## Standalone

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Off the main flow entirely.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - **`/grill-me`** — the same relentless interview as `/grill-with-docs`, but for when you have **no codebase**. Stateless: it saves nothing locally, builds no `CONTEXT.md`. Reach for it to sharpen any plan or design that doesn't live in a repo.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - **`/prototype`** — a small, throwaway program that answers one design question: does this state model feel right, or what should this UI look like. Throwaway from day one — keep the answer, delete the code. It's the detour in step 2 of the main flow, but reach for it any time a design question is hard to settle on paper.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - **`/research`** — delegate reading legwork to a **background agent**: it investigates a question against **primary sources**, then leaves a cited Markdown file in the repo. Keep working while it reads. The file it produces is something to take *into* the main flow at `/grill-with-docs` — research feeds the thinking, it doesn't replace it.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - **`/teach`** — learn a concept over multiple sessions, using the current directory as a stateful workspace.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - **`/writing-great-skills`** — reference for writing and editing skills well.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ## Precondition

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: **`/setup-matt-pocock-skills`** — run before your first engineering flow to configure the issue tracker, triage labels, and doc layout the other skills assume. Custom issue trackers also work.
